question: Can a grant containing drive.readonly plus drive.file be mistaken for permission to write an entire existing Drive collection?
kind: Pre-registered fail-before-fix synthetic scope regression control; no Google API request or cloud mutation
isolation: The old grant validator with the new assertion is in .local-state/worktrees/google-default-oauth-negative. Each worktree uses its own Cargo target. Do not compile while the one-hour Shared Drive measurement is running.
arms: A: run google_login_uses_pkce_loopback_offline_consent_and_explicit_scopes against the old validator; require failure on drive.readonly plus drive.file
B: run the same test against the changed validator; require rejection of that grant and acceptance of the full drive scope
endpoint: Count the correction only if A fails on the new scope assertion and B passes, with the expected test executed in each worktree. Then run the full repository check before committing.
prediction: The old predicate accepts the combined limited scopes as writable; the corrected predicate requires the full drive scope for a writable whole-collection mount.

result.baseline: The single selected cirrove-auth unit test in the negative-control worktree failed at the new assertion: the old validator accepted openid plus drive.readonly plus drive.file for ReadWrite. The runner reported 1 failed, 13 filtered out; exit 101.
result.changed: The same selected test in the feature worktree passed, rejecting that limited combination and accepting full drive. The runner reported 1 passed, 14 filtered out; exit 0. A separate synthetic refresh test for the public Desktop client without a client secret also passed (1 passed, 14 filtered out).
result.commands: Both worktrees ran cargo test -p cirrove-auth --lib --locked google_login_uses_pkce_loopback_offline_consent_and_explicit_scopes -- --nocapture with distinct CARGO_TARGET_DIR values. The feature worktree additionally ran the filtered google_public_desktop_client_refreshes_without_a_client_secret test.
